Since Rails resource update routes still accept PATCH, an existing client sending PATCH with changes would fall into the new `update`, which saves only alias_level/visible/name and renders success_json — silently ignoring membership changes and returning success. adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous PATCH-based incremental membership update path in Admin::GroupsController (update_patch reading params[:changes] with add/delete) and replaces update with a method that only handles alias_level/visible/name from top-level params. Routes still provide the standard update route (so PATCH requests would still be routed to update), but now any PATCH request sending changes: {add/delete} will have those params ignored and can still return success_json if the group saves, resulting in a silent no-op for membership changes. Additionally, routes.rb removes the old admin groups `get "users"` route and introduces PUT/DELETE `members` routes instead, so clients using the old endpoints/semantics will break.
